html:
Samoa skipped 30 December 2011: the country went from Thursday the 29th straight to Saturday the 31st, moving itself west of the International Date Line.

Since 1892 Samoa had kept the same day as the United States, whose traders then mattered most. By 2011 its main partners were New Zealand and Australia, and being a day behind them cost two working days a week.

The change put Samoa among the first places to see each new day, while American Samoa, a few kilometres east, stayed among the last. It followed a similar move by Kiribati in 1995.
sum: Samoa skipped 30 December 2011: the country went from Thursday the 29th straight to Saturday the 31st, moving itself west of the International Date Line.
